title: Optimal polynomial-time approximation ratio for asymmetric TSP
area: Approximation algorithms and hardness of approximation
formal: Determine \(\rho_{\mathrm{ATSP}}\), the infimum of achievable expected polynomial-time approximation ratios for the asymmetric metric traveling salesman problem.
definitions: An instance is an integer \(n\ge3\) and a full rational directed-distance matrix \(d\in\mathbb Q_{\ge0}^{n\times n}\) with \(d(i,i)=0\), strictly positive off-diagonal entries, and \(d(i,k)\le d(i,j)+d(j,k)\) for every triple. Symmetry is not required. A feasible directed tour is a permutation \(\pi\) of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), of cost \(\sum_{i=1}^{n}d(\pi(i),\pi(i+1))\), where \(\pi(n+1)=\pi(1)\). OPT is the minimum tour cost. An algorithm is a uniform randomized Turing machine with independent fair random bits. Its worst-case running time, over all random tapes, is polynomial in the binary input length. It always returns a feasible solution, and its expected cost is measured over its coins. A real number \(r\ge1\) is achievable if one such algorithm satisfies \(\mathbb E[\operatorname{cost}(A(I))]\le r\operatorname{OPT}(I)\) for every valid instance I. The target is the infimum of achievable r; the polynomial and algorithm may depend on r. An infimum need not be attained. All integers and rational input data use explicit binary encodings, with numerator and positive denominator for each rational; their full lengths count toward the input size. No complexity assumption is built into the definition.

context_blocks.text: Directional costs prevent treating the tour as an undirected object. Constant-factor approximation is now known, leaving the optimal constant as the main unrestricted algorithmic target.

The March 2026 preprint improves the ratio below fifteen. This card concerns arbitrary polynomial-time algorithms; the separate subtour-LP integrality-gap card concerns the strength of a fixed relaxation.

why: Determine the efficient-approximation threshold for directed routing, a central remaining question after the constant-factor ATSP breakthrough.

references.title: Better approximation guarantee for Asymmetric TSP
references.locator: Abstract and main approximation theorem; a ratio below fifteen.

progress.text: Vygen reports a polynomial-time approximation ratio below fifteen, together with improved relaxation bounds.

answer_criterion: Supply a real number a and a complete Lean-checked proof that its absolute difference from the defined constant is at most \(1/100\). A proved containing interval of width at most \(1/50\) qualifies through its midpoint. The constant is unconditional: a lower bound relying on an unproved complexity assumption settles only the corresponding conditional statement. Merely restating the defining infimum is not a determination.

sentences: Asymmetric TSP allows different costs for the two directions between a pair of vertices.
The costs obey the directed triangle inequality and the output visits each vertex once in a cycle.
The target is the best expected ratio among all uniform randomized polynomial-time algorithms.
A March 2026 result improves the known constant without determining this infimum.
The benchmark requires a certified estimate within absolute error 0.01.
